plan.summary: Add a BACKWARD movement order that moves a vehicle one grid cell opposite its current orientation while preserving orientation and applying the existing boundary, simultaneous-movement, and collision rules.
steps: Add BACKWARD to the MovementOrder enum.
Add an opposite-direction operation to Direction so reverse movement can reuse Position.move without duplicating coordinate logic.
Handle BACKWARD in MovementEngine.applyOrder by moving once in the orientation opposite to the vehicle's current orientation without changing that orientation.

Keep reverse movement within the existing intention and conflict-resolution flow so board boundaries, occupied cells, competing targets, swaps, and dependent blocking behave consistently with forward movement.
Update the game rules to list and define BACKWARD, describe its movement vectors and boundary behavior, and remove reverse movement from the out-of-scope list.
tests: Extend MovementEngineTest to verify backward movement for NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, and WEST and confirm orientation is unchanged.
Verify a backward move that would leave the board is blocked.
Verify backward movement into a stationary vehicle is blocked.
Verify backward orders participate correctly in simultaneous target conflicts and position-swap blocking.
Run the backend test suite with ./mvnw test from the backend directory.
